issues.legal_issue: The death of a claimant does not require dismissal of an entire appeal when the remaining claimants assert distinct, independent rights and relief for them can be granted without producing an unenforceable or contradictory decree.
material_facts: The compensation apportionment proceedings involved claimants asserting specified, separate shares in the acquired land.
The claimants’ separate claims were heard together and decided in consolidated proceedings.
Five appellants died during the High Court appeals, and their legal representatives were not brought on record within time.
Other appellants had surviving claims based on their own shares, which they could have pursued separately.
The High Court treated the appeals as wholly abated and also dismissed connected appeals raising similar issues.
issues.conclusion: The appeals did not abate in their entirety merely because the claims of some deceased appellants could not be continued; the surviving appellants’ claims could proceed, and the High Court’s contrary orders were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 22 of the Code of Civil Procedure, abatement against one party does not automatically abate an appeal against others. Whether an appeal can continue depends on the nature of the rights, claims, relief, and decree, including whether granting relief to the surviving parties would make the decree unenforceable or contradictory to a decree that has become final. The Court applied the principles in Nathu Ram v. State of Punjab, Ram Sarup v. Munshi, Harihar Prasad Singh v. Balmiki Prasad Singh, and Indian Oxygen Ltd. v. Ram Adhar Singh, distinguishing cases involving joint and indivisible rights. Sections 11, 18, 30 and 31 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, support treating compensation apportionment as a determination of the respective entitlements of interested persons.

rule.if: compensation_apportionment_appeal and claimants_assert_independent_shares and claims_consolidated_for_convenience and some_claimants_unrepresented_after_death and surviving_relief_independently_enforceable

predicates.compensation_apportionment_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning the allocation of compensation among persons claiming an interest in acquired property.
predicates.claimants_assert_independent_shares: The claimants assert distinct shares or rights that do not depend on one another.
predicates.claims_consolidated_for_convenience: Separate claims are joined or decided together for convenience or because they raise similar issues.
predicates.some_claimants_unrepresented_after_death: One or more claimants die during the proceeding and their legal representatives are not brought on record.
predicates.surviving_relief_independently_enforceab: Relief for the remaining claimants can be enforced without negating or making unenforceable relief that has become final for another claimant.

issues.definition: When an compensation-allocation appeal involves consolidated but independent claims, and relief for the remaining claimants remains independently enforceable, the appeal may continue for them despite the absence of representatives for deceased claimants.

issues.legal_issue: A court should take a liberal and reasonable approach to delay in bringing legal representatives on record when refusing substitution would prevent adjudication of other claimants’ independent rights on the merits.
material_facts: The High Court appeals remained pending when applications were made to bring the deceased appellants’ legal representatives on record.
The applications were delayed, and the High Court rejected the requests to condone the delay and set aside abatement.
The surviving appellants had independent claims, and dismissing their appeals would prevent their claims from being decided on the merits.
issues.conclusion: The High Court should have condoned the delay and allowed the deceased appellants’ legal representatives to be brought on record; its rejection of those applications was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Order 22 of the Code of Civil Procedure is a flexible procedural tool intended to facilitate effective adjudication, not to defeat substantial rights. Procedural rules are the handmaid of justice, and the Court should adopt a liberal approach to delay where dismissal would foreclose adjudication of independent claims. The Court relied on the principles in Harihar Prasad Singh v. Balmiki Prasad Singh and Indian Oxygen Ltd. v. Ram Adhar Singh, and invoked the maxim actus curiae neminem gravabit.

rule.if: pending_appeal and delayed_substitution_application and deceased_claimant_had_independent_claim and refusal_would_block_merits_for_surviving_claimants

predicates.pending_appeal: The appeal remains pending before the court when substitution is sought.
predicates.delayed_substitution_application: An application to bring a deceased party’s legal representatives on record is filed after the applicable time.
predicates.deceased_claimant_had_independent_claim: The deceased party asserted a right or claim distinct from those of the other parties.
predicates.refusal_would_block_merits_for_surviving: Rejecting substitution would prevent surviving parties from obtaining a decision on their own claims.

issues.definition: When a delayed substitution application arises in a pending appeal and refusal would block merits adjudication of other parties’ independent claims, the delay should be condoned and substitution allowed.

issues.legal_issue: Persons seeking to enter appellate proceedings after the hearing has concluded may be refused impleadment when their predecessor was not a party before the courts below.
material_facts: After the hearing had concluded and orders had been reserved, applicants claiming an interest in the compensation sought impleadment.
Their predecessor had not been a party before either the Reference Court or the High Court.
issues.conclusion: The applications for impleadment were rejected.
issues.legal_principle: The Court found no justification to entertain the late-stage impleadment applications in the circumstances presented, because the applicants’ predecessor had not participated as a party in the proceedings before the courts below. The judgment does not cite a specific provision or earlier case for this ruling.

predicates.appellate_impleadment_application: A person applies to be added as a party in an appellate proceeding.
predicates.predecessor_not_party_below: The applicant’s predecessor was not a party in the proceedings before the lower courts.
predicates.application_made_after_hearing_reserved: The application is made after the hearing is complete and the court has reserved its decision.

issues.definition: An appellate impleadment application may be rejected when the applicant’s predecessor was not a party below and the application is made after the hearing has concluded.
